editorial:
If you're looking for a cozy holiday movie to share with the kids, this Barbie take on the classic Charles Dickens tale is a sweet pick. The story kicks off when Kelly doesn't want to go to a Christmas Eve ball, so Barbie steps in with a story about Eden Starling, a glamorous singing diva in Victorian England who owns a theatre and only cares about herself. Eden is basically the Scrooge of this world, complete with a snooty cat named Chuzzlewit, and she forces her employees to work on Christmas. The animation is bright and colorful, and the Victorian setting gives it a charming storybook feel that keeps things lively without getting too heavy.

The voice acting is solid, especially Eden's dramatic personality, and the pacing moves along nicely so younger viewers won't get bored. On the downside, the songs are a bit forgettable and the plot follows the original story pretty closely, so there aren't many surprises. Still, it's a fun, family-friendly way to introduce kids to a classic tale. If you want to watch, you can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Eden is visited by three spirits who show her the past, present, and future. She sees how lonely and unhappy her future will be if she keeps her selfish ways. Waking up on Christmas morning, Eden has a change of heart. She rushes to her employees, gives them the day off, and even invites them to celebrate with her. She also reconnects with her old friend Catherine, who she had pushed away. The twist is that Eden realizes Christmas isn't about gifts or fame, but about kindness and sharing time with the people you love. She ends the story as a warmer, happier person.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family-friendly holiday stories and classic tales retold for kids.
